And really hard to get for a beginner. The songs go through strumming on one or all four but don’t really put it together in a way that is musical. I am new to all of this and am really not complaining because the app has endless tools and tutorials but is missing that one element. Maybe choose a fun song everyone should learn from each chapter and piece by piece go through it the way it was intended. Easy songs are not easy for someone just starting out. It is very difficult to keep pushing forward without real success even if it is a simple nursery rhyme that is fun to play. I have complemented this with some other online videos which has helped put some of the puzzle pieces together. All in all the app is great and even better if you pair it with his online content, I wish it was all in one place and the videos were paired with the song tutorials in some way.

Structured, Motivating, and Actually Makes Progress Measurable. Justin’s teaching style and the structure of the app are excellent. The focus on rhythm and timing early on makes a huge difference, and the clear progression goals like hitting 30 chord changes per minute before moving on are incredibly motivating and effective.

You can tell the lessons are built from real teaching experience. Techniques are introduced in a way that helps things “click” faster instead of feeling overwhelming. I also like the daily practice feedback that shows stats like how much time you’ve spent playing it’s a great reinforcement for consistency.

One feature I’d love to see added is an overall progress dashboard with long-term stats, practice streaks, and a skill or technique matrix to track growth over time. That would take an already great app to the next level.

But it makes it fun, and I even enjoy playing songs that I never really liked all that well, and there’s some favorites in here as well. Justin is very methodical in his approach, not focusing on just one thing, but layering more and more things in, in a very complete way it feels. It’s not just add another cord, but it’s strumming patterns, finger stretching, he introduces note picking pretty early on. Each set of lessons adds another layer that I have to practice before I move on, so the pace does slow down, but that’s OK. It’s important to have a good foundation and this app seems to give you that. I’m in it until the last lesson.

It doesn’t matter how much you update your software, if you try to use the wasd keys, etc… Across several apple devices if it isn’t on an iPhone you can’t scroll. You can’t see all the lessons and hence can’t complete them. Google chrome is tough as well as the “login with google account” option disappears when using the internet (which is how I login elsewhere) so you simple can’t login their either. Great App..but. Learning on this app is fun and there is tons of great material here. The downfall is chord recognition on the changes. It really throws me off if I look at the screen when doing changes as it freezes and stops counting.

The core is great, but there are enough inconsistencies with the other material it can be frustrating. The app has different chords for Wonderwall than the lesson, for example. Some songs have the strum pattern, others just have 4/4. Somewhere in the Orange is notated as a bar of 3/4 followed by a bar of 4/4.

Once I got to a certain level I started with an in-person teacher to get more personalized instruction, but I always come back to this app for review of basics- and continuing on the path in between live lessons- I always get more tidbits when I watch the videos a 2nd time. Justin is a master at relating to the viewer and really breaking steps down so anyone can learn. Highly problematic on Mac. Justin is an outstanding teacher, and his lessons are top notch. The content is a solid 5/5. But the current version of the app is 1/5 on Mac. It's absolutely burning up my CPU. I noticed when it ate through my 2023 Macbook Pro Max's battery in just a few hours (should last 12-18). Activity Monitor shows the app is constantly using 205% of CPU, and the energy impact score is 5440. For reference, this is about 11x the energy impact of Firefox with tons of tabs open, including an active Youtube tab, or several times the energy use of Cubase 13 Pro with a giant orchestral project loaded up. This is whether the app is in use, or just minimized. Either there's a serious glitch (most likely), or somebody hacked the app and injected it with crypto mining code. Moving on from that huge technical issue, the app could really benefit from mouse scrolling and basic keyboard controls (play/pause, skip back, skip forward, go back) on Mac. Finally, the videos are extremely loud and there's no way to control the volume of the app itself. I run my electric guitar through an interface (which outputs it through the same speakers as Justin), so it's not like I can simply turn down the system volume. I have to choose between having Justin at an acceptable volume but barely hearing my guitar, or absolutely cranking my guitar's gain, which destroys the sound quality.
